targetText: On the one hand, it would be a fatal mistake to declare that since there is a discrepancy between our economic “forces” and our political strength, it “follows” that we should not have seized power.[4] Such an argument can be advanced only by a “man in a muffler”,[5] who forgets that there will always be such a “discrepancy”, that it always exists in the development of nature as well as in the development of society, that only by a series of attempts: each of which, taken by itself, will be one sided and will suffer from certain inconsistencies: will complete socialism be created by the revolutionary co-operation of the proletarians of all countries.
summary: Refusing to seize political power until economic conditions are 'perfect' is mechanical dogmatism; uneven development is universal in nature and history.
explanation: Lenin refutes both Menshevik determinism (which claimed Russia was too economically backward for revolution) and ultra-left impatience, showing that proletarian state power can be used to consciously accelerate material development.

targetText: No. Only those are worthy of the name of Communists who understand that it is impossible to create or introduce socialism without learning from the organisers of the trusts. For socialism is not a figment of the imagination, but the assimilation and application by the proletarian vanguard, which has seized power, of what has been created by the trusts.
summary: Socialism is not an idealist figment of the imagination, but the working class's practical appropriation and mastery of large-scale organization created by capitalism.
explanation: Against the idealist fantasy that socialism can be invented out of pure revolutionary willpower without technical expertise, Lenin insists that the proletarian state must employ and learn from first-class technical specialists under workers' oversight.

targetText:
Bukharin noted and emphasised that the old state machinery must be “smashed” and “blown up”, that the bourgeoisie must be “finally and completely strangled” and so on. The frenzied petty bourgeoisie may also want this. And this, in the main, is what our revolution has already done between October 1917 and February 1918.

In my pamphlet I also mention what even the most revolutionary petty bourgeois cannot want, what the class-conscious proletarian does want, what our revolution has not yet accomplished. On this task, the task of tomorrow, Bukharin said nothing.
summary: While petty-bourgeois revolutionaries focus only on smashing the old order, proletarian revolutionaries must also build disciplined accounting, control, and labor organization.
explanation: Lenin highlights the decisive boundary between anarchistic or ultra-left destruction and Marxist-Leninist construction: smashing the bourgeois state is only the first step toward building a disciplined socialist economy.
